{{nihongo|'''Makoto Kumada'''|熊田 誠|Kumada Makoto|17 January 1920 – 28 June 2007}} was a Japanese [[chemist]] and was a Professor of Chemistry first at [[Osaka City University]] until his retirement in 1983 at  [[Kyoto University]] in [[Japan]]. In 1972, Kumada's group reported nickel-catalyzed cross coupling reactions nearly concurrently with the Corriu group working in France. The [[Kumada coupling]] now bears his name.

In an interview after the 2010 [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] was announced, Nobel Committee member Jan Bekvall (professor at [[Stockholm University]]) said: "If Professor Kumada been alive, he could have won this year's Nobel Prize for his work in developing cross-coupling."
